question: What may an organization being onboarded see of other organizations (the federations and congresses it could join, the member counts of its peers, the clauses other organizations shared), and is any of it a declared public directory or does each item need the other organization to opt in?
decision: Publish only federation/congress name, region and explicitly approved directory attributes. No organization counts or identifiable details by default. Benchmarks require affirmative opt-in by source organizations, at least 10 contributing organizations, cell-level suppression and anti-reidentification checks; small-union outliers must be suppressed even where n>=10. Clauses require source publication authorization and disclosure review; anonymize unless the source explicitly permits attribution.
originalProposedDecision: A declared public directory: federations and congresses list name and province only, never member counts. Peer benchmarks are aggregates of at least 5 opted-in orgs. Shared clauses appear only if the source org shared them publicly, and anonymized.
